title: Camp (canonical entity file)
description: One file per camp property: data/camps/<slug>.json. Registry + classification + history layer only — operational data (sessions, fees, dates, availability) stays in camp-finder / the council's own site, joined by camp id. A camp is classified on three orthogonal facets: camp_type (what kind of place, single), program_types (what it offers, set), and operator (+council; who runs it). Camp identity is independent of council ownership (camps change hands): council/operator are versioned attributes; sales/transfers are 'transferred' events, closures 'discontinued' events in data/camps/_events.json. Slugs keep camp-finder's state-prefixed convention (e.g. 'or-camp-meriwether').

camp_type.description: Primary structural classification (single; open vocab). Canonical set: reservation (a multi-camp property), resident_camp, high_adventure_base, short_term_camp (weekend/primitive troop use), day_camp, program_center, other. Multi-use is expressed via program_types, not here.

operator.description: Ownership/operation tier. 'council' pairs with the council ref below; 'national' = a National Council property (e.g. Philmont, Florida Sea Base, Northern Tier, Summit Bechtel) with council null. Disambiguates a null council (national base vs genuinely unknown).

council.description: Owning/operating council during this window; null = unknown (common for historical camps).

parent.description: The reservation this camp belongs to, as a camp ref (a sub-camp of a scout reservation); null if standalone. Reservation children are populated in a later pass.

operating_status.description: camp-finder semantics: 'not_operating' = property exists but no program; 'closed' = property gone/sold.

geo_precision.description: Confidence of lat/lon: 'exact' = camp-specific source point inside its state box; 'approximate' = city or state-centroid backfill (tools/geocode_camps.py); null = could not be placed. Consumers should soft-plot or bucket 'approximate' points.

elevation_ft.description: Ground elevation at lat/lon in feet above sea level (Copernicus 90m DEM via open-meteo, tools/elevation.py), rounded to the nearest 10 ft. Inherits geo_precision: for an 'approximate' point this is the city/reservation-centroid elevation, not the camp's exact ground. null when lat/lon is null.

july_high_f.description: Average daily high temperature in July in °F — a WorldClim v2.1 climate normal for 1970-2000, sampled at 30 arc-seconds (~1 km) from the camp's coordinate (tools/july_temp.py). Inherits geo_precision: for an 'approximate' point this describes the city/reservation centroid. A coastal or island camp whose cell is open water uses the nearest land cell. July is a fixed month (US resident-camp season) — still a real July value for overseas/equatorial camps, but not necessarily their camp season. null when lat/lon is null.

july_low_f.description: Average overnight low temperature in July in °F — companion to july_high_f (same source, window, and caveats).

website.description: Authoritative council/camp page during this window.

program_types.description: Programs/audiences offered here (open vocab, multi-valued): scouts_bsa_resident, cub_resident, cub_day, webelos, high_adventure, short_term_camping, venturing, sea_scout, family_camping, training. A single property is often multi-use.

features.description: What this camp offers — facilities, activities, accommodation, and program models — as coded entries from the open `camp-features` vocabulary. ONE namespace holds both widely-shared features (dining_hall) and long-tail differentiators (land_sailing): `code` is the only filterable key, and the vocabulary's `broader` field lets a consumer roll specific leaves up to coarse parents. Records only WHETHER the property offers something; dates, fees, session schedules, and availability stay at the council site. Always read alongside `features_verified_at` — an empty array by itself does NOT mean the camp offers none. Codes are unique per version (enforced by tools/validate_data.py).

signature.description: This camp presents the feature as a headline draw — a reason to travel here. Deliberately per camp rather than per vocabulary term, because the same feature is table stakes in one region and a differentiator in another (a climbing tower in Colorado vs on the prairie).

note.description: Optional short factual phrase for cases where the code alone under-describes the offering (e.g. 'Land sailers and sandboards on two miles of private beach'). Evergreen and non-promotional: no dates, fees, or session schedules; enforced by tools/validate_data.py.

features_verified_at.description: Date of the last deliberate features survey of this camp against its own sources — what makes `features` interpretable. The two vary independently: null + [] = never surveyed, nothing known; null + entries = incidental data from a bulk import, not a survey; date + entries = surveyed; date + [] = surveyed and the camp genuinely offers none of the vocabulary's features. Without this an unsurveyed camp is indistinguishable from an empty one, every 'has X' filter silently under-reports, and 'camps without X' is unanswerable.

features_source_tier.description: How good the source behind `features` was — a completeness qualifier, in the same spirit as `geo_precision` for coordinates. `guide`: a camp-specific DOCUMENT was read (leader's or program guide, program schedule, or a labelled camp map) — the most complete source available, averaging 21 features per camp. `camp_page`: a descriptive web page owned by the camp or its council, averaging 13. `portal`: ONLY a registration-platform blurb was available because the camp has no descriptive page anywhere; these are deliberately thin, are the least complete surveys in the dataset, and form the standing queue for manual review. `null` iff `features_verified_at` is null (coupling enforced by tools/validate_data.py). A `portal` survey is still a real survey — the date means a source was read — but treat its feature list as a floor, not a description. Derived mechanically from which provenance sources carry an `accessed` date, biased so `guide` is never over-claimed.

summary.description: Evergreen, original-prose description (setting, size, and the kinds of programs offered). MUST NOT contain dates, fees, session schedules, or other transitory details; enforced by tools/validate_data.py.

merged_from.description: Retired camp ids that resolve to this camp: program/session variants of the same physical property collapsed in, or a prior id this camp was renamed from. Any unioned programs/features live here; consumers resolve old ids via v1/camps/aliases.json.

reservation.description: Set when this camp shares a location with other distinct camps (a reservation centroid): a grouping so consumers render one reservation pin per property. `name` is null when the camps carry no common reservation name. Not a plottable entity. `id` is a STABLE OPAQUE GROUPING KEY — deliberately a bare slug, NOT a '{kind}:{slug}' EntityRef, because no reservation entity exists (contrast `council`, which is a real ref). Should a reservation dataset ever be added, it will reuse these exact slugs as its entity ids and any reference will arrive as a NEW additive field — this `id` will not change format or meaning. Group by it; do not parse it.
